target_customer: Recreational and competitive cyclists who pay a monthly or annual subscription for ride analysis and training guidance
problem: Cyclists have ride data scattered across Strava, Garmin, Zwift and Peloton and no personalized, affordable coaching that turns it into training guidance.
business_model: Consumer subscription ($7.99 per month or $89.99 per year in June 2021)
product_category: Cycling training and performance coaching app

founders.name: Jordan Kobert
previous_startups: Urbandoor (acquired by Airbnb, per YC page)
founders.background_notes: Described by the Fitt Insider Q&A (2022-01-03) as one of the first 10 Strava employees. Education not found.

founders.name: Christian Vande Velde
founders.background_notes: Former Tour de France rider and longtime friend of Kobert. Listed as a co-founder in a Terra podcast episode title and a coaching partner in the Fitt Insider Q&A; the YC page does not list him.

exit.reason: Strava bought the core assets; terms not disclosed; the standalone app is to be folded into Strava

competitors.name: Zwift
competitors.what: Indoor cycling platform with structured workouts and rider profiling that the review says could add similar coaching features
competitors.funding_then: Not stated in the source (the funding press release notes Zwift's recent funding came from some of the same investors)

competitors.name: The Sufferfest
competitors.what: Structured training app with a four dimensional power profile

competitors.name: Strava
competitors.what: Ride logging and social network whose history The Breakaway reads; also the founders' former employer and the later acquirer

technical_complexity.rationale: Aggregating ride data from Strava, Garmin, Zwift and Peloton through APIs and computing power interval analysis was standard engineering for a two engineer team that started in fall 2020, with the analytics the harder part.

defensibility.rationale: The app read data other platforms owned, and Zwift or Strava could add similar metrics. Differentiation rested on analysis quality and a pro cyclist as coaching face, neither hard to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Strava, the founders' former employer, bought the core assets in May 2025 about a month after buying Runna, and plans to retire the standalone app.

market_need_then: Pandemic era growth in cycling and indoor training. The Fitt Insider Q&A (2022-01) cites a total market in the hundreds of millions of people, and a June 2021 review shows demand for deeper power analysis than Zwift offered.

branding.domain_note: Company site used breakaway.app, not an exact .com, per YC listing.

identity.logo: Not described by any opened source
identity.voice_and_tone: Performance and insight oriented; positions itself as a personal coach and companion

branding.brand_signature: Christian Vande Velde, a former Tour de France rider, as the coaching face
branding.community_and_virality: Growth reportedly relied on word of mouth, coach partners and paid ads; no meme or merch evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: Niche cycling brand with coverage in cycling press and a pro rider tie in, but no evidence of broad awareness before being absorbed by Strava.

pivots.from: Data and insights app with recorded coaching content
pivots.why: Company introduced an AI coach feature in October 2023 per search coverage; reason not stated

outcome_analysis: Two former Strava employees started The Breakaway in fall 2020, joined YC in Summer 2021 and raised a $2.9M seed in February 2022. It stayed small, with a six person team in the directory, and Strava bought its core assets in May 2025 without disclosed terms. The outcome is a soft strategic exit rather than a venture scale result, and the YC directory still lists the company as Active.
notes: Company site breakaway.app returned HTTP 503 when fetched.
